source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyaya 20: in his time Garuda breaks out of his egg, huge and blazing like a heap of fire, and rises into the sky; the gods, taking his blaze for Agni's, run to Agni (Vibhavasu), who tells them it is Garuda, son of Vinata, his equal in splendour; the gods praise Garuda, who draws in his radiance; he goes to his mother and finds her a slave (1.20–21).
structure: From episode 11: COLD OPEN (the hook over the episode's strongest image, big on-screen text from frame 1; KIT.series.hookCard) → title (the hook's post) → RECAP (≈2.5 s) → STORY (with a brief cut to Sauti at the Naimisha fire) → the cliffhanger image + line → a silent ≈1.5 s Next card that dissolves back into the first frame (KIT.series.loopNextScene).

strings.garudaEpithet: king of birds, son of Vinata

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Who was born so bright that the gods thought the world was burning?
lines.say: Who was born so bright [p:60] that the gods thought the world was burning?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (moving from frame 1): Garuda rising out of a burst of fire, wings opening, blazing gold against a red sky; the question in big text from frame 1.

lines.text: Vinata lost the wager, and became her sister's slave.
lines.say: Vinata lost the wager, [p:80] and became her sister's slave.
lines.note: RECAP: episode 18's image as a memory: Vinata bowed in slavery, Kadru standing over her.

lines.text: In his own time, the second egg broke open.
lines.say: In his own time, [p:100] the second egg broke open.
lines.note: STORY 1: Kashyapa's hermitage before dawn, the gold egg in its jar; on 'broke' (beats[1]) it splits and fire pours out.

lines.text: Out came Garuda: huge, blazing like a heap of fire, rising into the sky.
lines.say: Out came Garuda: [p:150] huge, [p:80] blazing like a heap of fire, [p:80] rising into the sky.
lines.note: STORY 2 · REVEAL: Garuda rises LARGE out of the fire, wings opening (beats[0] name card); the whole frame burns gold (blaze); he lifts into the sky (beats[3]).

lines.text: The gods were afraid, and ran to Agni, the god of fire.
lines.say: The gods were afraid, [p:80] and ran to Agni, the god of fire.
lines.note: STORY 3: Indra's heaven under a burning sky (EP8.svarga, reddened): the gods hurry toward Agni, whose seven tongues of fire rise behind him; name card.

lines.speaker: agni
lines.text: "This is not my fire. It is Garuda, Vinata's son, as bright as I am."
lines.say: This is not my fire. [p:150] It is Garuda, [p:80] Vinata's son, [p:80] as bright as I am.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %): after a 350 ms rest, Agni speaks (direct speech), LARGE, pointing out across the sky at the distant blaze.

lines.text: So the gods praised Garuda, and asked him to spare them.
lines.say: So the gods praised Garuda, [p:100] and asked him to spare them.
lines.note: STORY 5: the gods with folded hands (bow) before Garuda, who hangs in the sky, wings spread, blazing.

lines.text: He heard them, and drew in his fire.
lines.say: He heard them, [p:120] and drew in his fire.
lines.note: STORY 6: the blaze draws back into him (blaze 1 → 0), the sky cools to dawn colours; he folds his wings halfway (beats[1]).

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then the great bird flew home, to his mother.
lines.say: Then the great bird flew home, [p:80] to his mother.
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti at the Naimisha fire, an eighth angle: from high above the clearing, the fire a small sun; a bird's shadow passes over the sages).

lines.text: He found Vinata, and learned that she was a slave.
lines.say: He found Vinata, [p:150] and learned that she was a slave.
lines.note: STORY 7: the shore; Garuda alights before Vinata, who kneels with her head covered (slave); he bows to her; on 'slave' (beats[1]) Kadru's shadow falls across them both.

lines.text: And his first task as a slave's son: to carry the serpents.
lines.say: And his first task as a slave's son: [p:200] to carry the serpents.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger image): Kadru points; a heap of her serpent sons rears before Garuda, who looks at them, his eye burning.
The short, silent Next card: a glimpse of episode 20: Garuda flying high with serpents on his back toward the sun; then the loop back to frame 1.
